title: Home or hemma? Going somewhere vs being somewhere
goal: Choose the right form of the little place words — *hem* or *hemma*, *ut* or *ute*, *upp* or *uppe* — depending on whether you are moving or staying put.
bekal: seven pairs of direction and location words: *hem/hemma*, *in/inne*, *ut/ute*, *upp/uppe*, *ner/nere*, *bort/borta*, *fram/framme*
talking about the rooms and spaces of a Swedish apartment building
wave: Go back to Unit 3: say ten particle verbs aloud with the stress on the particle — *gå UT*, *komma IN*, *ta PÅ sig* — then notice how many of today's words are those very particles.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Förstärkaren i källaren
dialogs.intro: A Saturday afternoon in the flat on Södermalm. Jonas, Elin's younger brother, has a gig with his band tonight, and his amplifier is still down in the basement storage room. Dian is at home with a book — but not for long. A little later, Elin calls Jonas's phone.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Dian, är du hemma? Kan du hjälpa mig en stund?
lines.id: Dian, are you home? Can you help me for a minute?
lines.literal: Dian, are you at-home? can you help me a while?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, jag är här inne! Vad har hänt?
lines.id: Yes, I'm in here! What's happened?
lines.literal: yes, I am here inside! what has happened?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Vi har spelning ikväll, och förstärkaren står fortfarande nere i källaren.
lines.id: We have a gig tonight, and the amp is still down in the basement.
lines.literal: we have gig tonight, and amplifier-the stands still down-there in basement-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och du vill att jag ska hjälpa dig att bära upp den?
lines.id: And you want me to help you carry it up?
lines.literal: and you want that I shall help you to carry up it?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Precis. Bilen står ute på gatan, så vi bär ut den direkt.
lines.id: Exactly. The car's out on the street, so we'll carry it straight out.
lines.literal: exactly. car-the stands outside on street-the, so we carry out it directly.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej, vi går ner. Men var är nyckeln till förrådet?
lines.id: OK, let's go down. But where's the key to the storage room?
lines.literal: okay, we go down. but where is key-the to storage-room-the?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Den brukar hänga där borta vid dörren… Nej, den är borta!
lines.id: It usually hangs over there by the door… No, it's gone!
lines.literal: it usually-does hang there away by door-the… no, it is away!

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Haha, här är den. Tack. Kom, vi tar hissen ner.
lines.id: Ha ha, here it is. Thanks. Come on, let's take the elevator down.
lines.literal: haha, here is it. thanks. come, we take elevator-the down.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Puh, den var tyngre än jag trodde. Ska vi lyfta in den i bilen nu?
lines.id: Phew, it was heavier than I thought. Shall we lift it into the car now?
lines.literal: phew, it was heavier than I thought. shall we lift in it in car-the now?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Ja, in med den! Kommer du med till spelningen sen?
lines.id: Yes, in it goes! Are you coming along to the gig later?
lines.literal: yes, in with it! come you with to gig-the later?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna, men jag måste springa upp och byta om först.
lines.id: I'd love to, but I have to run up and change first.
lines.literal: gladly, but I must run up and change around first.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Jonas? Det är Elin. Jag är på väg hem. Är ni kvar hemma?
lines.id: Jonas? It's Elin. I'm on my way home. Are you still at home?
lines.literal: Jonas? it is Elin. I am on way home. are you(pl) remaining at-home?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Jag står här ute vid bilen, och Dian är uppe i lägenheten.
lines.id: I'm out here by the car, and Dian's up in the apartment.
lines.literal: I stand here outside by car-the, and Dian is up-there in apartment-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Bra, jag kommer fram om tio minuter. Åk inte härifrån utan mig!
lines.id: Good, I'll get there in ten minutes. Don't leave without me!
lines.literal: good, I come forward in ten minutes. drive not from-here without me!

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Skynda dig då. Vi måste vara framme vid sju.
lines.id: Hurry up, then. We have to be there by seven.
lines.literal: hurry yourself then. we must be at-the-front by seven.

notes: **Är du hemma? / Jag är på väg hem.** — the key pair of the unit. *Hem* is where you are **going** (direction), *hemma* is where you **are** (location). English says "home" in both cases ("go home", "be home"); Swedish adds an ending as soon as nothing is moving. The same goes for six more pairs: *in/inne*, *ut/ute*, *upp/uppe*, *ner/nere*, *bort/borta*, *fram/framme*. **HEM-mah**, **IN-neh**, **Ü-teh**, **ÜP-peh**, **NEH-reh**, **BOT-tah**, **FRAHM-meh**.

**Nere i källaren / uppe i lägenheten** — Swedes love to stack a location word in front of a place: *nere i källaren* (down in the basement), *uppe i lägenheten*, *ute på gatan*, *inne i köket*. It sounds a bit redundant to English ears, but leaving it out sounds flat. The same habit gives you *uppe i Norrland* (up north) and *nere i Skåne* (down south).

**Där borta / den är borta** — *borta* has two meanings: "over there, away" (*där borta vid dörren*) and "gone, missing" (*nyckeln är borta*). Jonas uses both within a few seconds. The direction form *bort* means "away": *gå bort*, *ta bort* (remove, delete) — a verb you will see on every computer screen.

**Framme** — "there, arrived" (at the destination). *Vi är framme!* is what Swedish parents say at the end of a car trip; *Vi måste vara framme vid sju* = we have to be there by seven. The direction form gives you *komma fram* (to arrive, to get there): *Jag kommer fram om tio minuter*.

**Kvar** — "still (there), left (over)": *Är ni kvar hemma?* (Are you still at home?), *Det finns kaffe kvar* (There's coffee left). It's one of those little words with no single English equivalent; think "remaining". **kvahr**.

**Byta om** — "to change (clothes)", literally "swap around". *Jag måste byta om* needs no object at all. And **härifrån** — from here — glues *här* and *ifrån* together; you'll meet its relatives *därifrån* and *hemifrån* below. **HEHR-ee-frohn**.

grammars.title: Seven pairs: moving or staying?
body: Ask yourself one question: **is something moving towards a place, or is it already there?** Moving → the short form. Staying, being, standing, lying, waiting → the long form. A third column adds *-ifrån* for "from".
after: **Movement verbs** that take the short form: *gå, åka, komma, springa, flytta, resa, bära, ta, lyfta, köra*. **Position verbs** that take the long form: *vara, bo, stå, ligga, sitta, stanna, vänta, jobba*. So: *Jag **stannar hemma*** (I'm staying home) but *Jag **åker hem*** (I'm going home).
*Ner* also exists in a more formal spelling, **ned**, and *nere* never changes. You'll see *ned* in written Swedish and on signs (*Nedgång* = way down, e.g. into the subway).

grammars.title: Here, there and where: the same split
body: You already know *här*, *där* and *var*. Each has a direction partner, and the logic is exactly the same as *hem/hemma*: moving towards → one form, being → another.
after: ***Var** bor du?* (where do you live?) — but ***Vart** ska du?* (where are you going?). English used to make the same distinction — "where" vs "whither", "here" vs "hither" — and simply lost it. Swedish kept it.

In everyday speech, many Swedes say *var* in both cases. You'll hear *Var ska du?* — but in writing, and in the speech of careful speakers, *vart* for direction is still the norm, and using it correctly will sound good.

blocks.text: Swedes describe their country vertically: you go **upp** to Norrland and **ner** to Skåne, and people living in Kiruna are *uppe i norr*. From Stockholm, Göteborg is *borta på västkusten* (over on the west coast). These words come out so naturally that you'll start using them yourself without thinking.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 3
items: Many particle verbs from Unit 3 use the direction forms as particles: *gå **ut***, *komma **in***, *ta **bort***, *sätta **upp***, *lägga **ner***.
The stress falls on the particle: *gå UT*, *ta BORT*, *bära UPP*.
Particles are always the short direction form — never *gå ute* or *bära uppe*. If it's a particle, it's moving.

blocks.text: Floors are counted differently from the US: *bottenvåningen* is the ground floor, and *första våningen* is often the floor above it — though in everyday speech many Swedes say *två trappor upp* (two flights up) instead. When someone gives you their address, ask for the *portkod* too, or you'll be standing outside.

The **tvättstuga** is a Swedish institution: a shared laundry room in the basement, booked in advance on a board or a screen. Forgetting to clean up after yourself — or taking someone else's slot — is a classic source of conflict between neighbors, and the subject of countless notes taped to the wall.

items: Vi / måste / framme / vara / sju / vid
Kan / bära / du / den / upp / hjälpa / mig / att
I'm going out to buy milk.

answers: hemma — in — ute — upp — nere — framme
Förstärkaren står nere i källaren. — Jag är på väg hem. — Vi måste vara framme vid sju. — Kan du hjälpa mig att bära upp den? — Jag väntar här ute.
Är det någon hemma? — Jag går ut och köper mjölk. — Vi kom fram klockan åtta. — Min cykel är borta! — Vart ska du? — Hon bor uppe i Norrland.
